scope.kv_layout: 32 layers, 8 KV heads, head dimension 128, 16-token blocks

baselines.name: Pinned llama.cpp upstream scheduler and contiguous KV path
comparability_limits: Only same model, prompts, seed, build type, and MSVC toolchain are comparable.
The pinned CPU upstream build is a semantic baseline; CUDA system comparisons use the fork's upstream policy mode.
Cross-compiler byte-identical output is not claimed.

baselines.name: Per-block cudaMemcpyAsync for mappings without snapshot requirements
comparability_limits: Direct copy is valid only when source and destination ranges do not require snapshot semantics.
It cannot be compared against Remap using a different mapping distribution.
Per-block copy launch count is part of the measured mechanism.

baselines.name: Scalar descriptor-driven Gather and Scatter
comparability_limits: Descriptors, staging, stream, and mapping must match Vector Remap exactly.
The two-kernel staging path is required for overlap semantics and is not comparable to a different Direct workload.
Current evidence covers one RTX 4050 Laptop GPU and the locked FP16 KV layout.

baselines.name: uint4 128-bit descriptor-driven Gather and Scatter
baselines.controlled_mode: snapshot-required mapping; uint4 Gather+Scatter with scalar fallback
comparability_limits: The 53.33% headline is a one-block Remap microbenchmark result, not end-to-end acceleration.
Aligned vector bytes and scalar fallback bytes must be reported separately.
This path materializes remapped KV and is not PagedAttention.

baselines.name: Same-math contiguous CUDA decode-attention comparator
baselines.controlled_mode: FP16 Q/K/V and FP32 online-softmax output with contiguous per-sequence K/V; identical CUDA math, launch geometry, inputs, seeds, stream, and timing boundary to paged K1
comparability_limits: This is a single-layer decode-attention microbenchmark comparator, not the upstream llama.cpp end-to-end attention graph.
It excludes page-table indirection but does not include Remap materialization, allocator, scheduler, model layers, or request latency.
Only the two preregistered Qwen2.5 geometries and the committed RTX 4050 protocol are quantitative evidence.

baselines.name: Deterministic rule-based benefit gate
comparability_limits: This is the mandatory simple heuristic, not an oracle and not a learned policy.
Fresh-process trials do not demonstrate long-lived adaptation.
Its current action is upstream versus CacheFlow scheduling, before the future five-action KV policy exists.

baselines.name: H0 deterministic legal-action fallback
baselines.controlled_mode: --kv-action-policy fixed; Direct -> device Swap -> host Swap -> Remap -> Paged -> Recompute after capability gates
comparability_limits: The formal CUDA run exposes only Direct, CUDA-managed Swap, transactional host Swap, and Recompute; Remap and Paged are masked.
All H0/A1/T1/L1 comparisons reuse the same paired scheduler snapshots and complete-action boundary.
Evidence is limited to one Qwen2.5-0.5B Q4_K_M model and one RTX 4050 Laptop GPU.

baselines.name: A1 analytical complete-action cost model
baselines.controlled_mode: --kv-action-policy analytical; bandwidth, launch, prefill, decode, reuse, and pressure terms evaluated on paired snapshots
comparability_limits: Analytical constants are protocol-locked and are not fitted on evaluation traces.
The production capability gate is applied before scoring, so masked Remap and Paged cannot win.
A tie with H0 is a neutral result, not evidence of model improvement.

baselines.name: T1 trace-safe bucketed lookup ablation
baselines.controlled_mode: offline median lookup keyed by action/context/batch/page-runs/pressure buckets on chronological train traces, evaluated on held-out paired traces
comparability_limits: T1 is an offline ablation and is not enabled as the production selector.
It intentionally uses literal bucket medians without a confidence gate to measure whether sparse table switching is unsafe.
Its result must be reported even when it is neutral or worse than H0.

baselines.name: L1 bounded per-action Ridge with H0 fallback
baselines.controlled_mode: --kv-action-policy learned-shadow during evidence collection; offline L1 applies minimum samples, residual uncertainty, confidence beta, switch margin, and exact H0 fallback
comparability_limits: The formal result is a safety/fallback result: L1 did not switch away from H0 on the held-out traces.
Shadow-mode recommendations are observable but do not alter the executed production action.
No claim is made that the current training sample establishes a learned-policy speedup.

baselines.name: FlashInfer candidate paged-KV batch decode kernel oracle
comparability_limits: It becomes a kernel comparator only after a pinned Linux or WSL environment and layout adapter pass correctness checks.
Only identical FP16 Q/K/V, GQA shape, page table, page size, context, and CUDA-event timing are comparable.
Kernel comparison cannot support an end-to-end server claim.

baselines.name: vLLM PagedAttention
comparability_limits: Different serving runtime, model format, allocator, scheduler, and kernel stack confound direct attribution.
The current Windows GGUF experiment matrix is not a supported like-for-like vLLM environment.
It is the conceptual and algorithmic reference until a pinned Linux environment and matched workload are available.

baselines.name: NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM paged KV cache
comparability_limits: TensorRT engines and supported deployment stacks differ from GGUF and llama.cpp.
End-to-end comparison would combine compiler, kernels, scheduler, and model-conversion effects.
Use as an implementation reference, not evidence for this project's quantitative claims.

baselines.name: FlexGen single-GPU offloading
comparability_limits: FlexGen targets latency-insensitive high-throughput offloading and OPT-family workloads.
Its weight, activation, and KV placement problem is broader than this project's decode-time KV action choice.
Retain as Swap and Recompute related work, not a matched performance baseline.
